exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean section)
outcome: Serum adiponectin and leptin levels at birth
Adiponectin and leptin gene expression at birth
Body mass index at 24 months postpartum
finding: Cesarean section was associated with lower maternal leptin levels at birth and shorter breastfeeding duration compared to vaginal delivery, while adiponectin levels and gene expression, and postpartum body mass index, did not differ between groups.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with lower maternal leptin levels at birth and shorter breastfeeding duration compared to vaginal delivery.
